lens: Accessible interaction — narrow mobile viewport; simulated AI review lens
reason: The sampled mobile public experience has a strong accessibility foundation: native links/buttons, visible labels, 44px-or-larger principal targets, a skip link, contrasting focus styles, and reduced-motion handling for the engagement instrument. The supplied 390px captures show coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy and stacked actions without apparent clipping. I traced the actual work-to-contact inquiry journey through source and its recorded synthetic browser check. The proposition identifies student-led consulting; contact explains pro-bono scope and confidentiality discussion, while home explicitly withholds unapproved case studies. Sampled application review copy accurately discloses identifying original resumes. However, contact validation recovery lacks field-specific guidance, and the supplied tests do not establish assistive-technology task completion. These are independent AI source/capture judgments, not observed human success or accessibility certification. Broad world-class agreement and integrated release readiness remain unproven.

findings.evidence: The API trims text and merges every invalid field into HTTP 400 with “Check the form fields and try again”. ContactForm renders that message only in the bottom alert; it neither passes FormField.error nor associates the server error with a control. For example, a whitespace-only name satisfies native required but becomes empty after server trimming. The browser journey test covers intercepted success only.
findings.userImpact: A narrow-screen or screen-reader visitor receives no identification of which field needs correction and must search and guess after submission. Native validation does not cover this server/client mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Return structured field errors for validation failures, pass them to FormField and the message textarea through aria-invalid/aria-describedby, and focus the first invalid field or a linked error summary. Add a focused whitespace-input rejection/recovery check.

notVerified: No browser was driven in this review. Supplied captures establish appearance only; keyboard traversal, sticky-header focus visibility, zoom/reflow and mobile virtual-keyboard behavior were not independently exercised.

The recorded menu test overrides the viewport to 820×600 even in its mobile project. It proves that sampled Escape/focus-return case, not complete keyboard navigation at 390px. Instrument tests verify selection and transition duration, not spoken live-region output.
No VoiceOver/TalkBack or desktop screen-reader evidence, physical-device, Safari or Firefox validation, or observed disabled-user task success is supplied.

No staging, hosted Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration or authenticated end-to-end acceptance exists. The contact confirmation uses intercepted HTTP; private application excerpts are source evidence only. Other private workflows were not comprehensively audited by this seat.
